messages:
Jill (Acme): Hey team — our free trial credits were almost exhausted overnight. We don't have interactive endpoints running; mainly a background indexer that calls embeddings + a rerank step. Usage graph shows a huge burst across embeddings and rerank between 02:00-05:00 UTC. Can someone check?

Sam (Support): Hi Jill — sorry to hear that. Can you share account id and a sample request/worker logs? Also did you see 429s or 5xxs in worker logs? I'll open a ticket.

infra-bot: Ticket TKT-4321 created and assigned to Sam (Support).

Jill (Acme): Account: acct_01G7x... Attached sanitized log snippet:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
payload: {"model":"rwd-embed-001","input": ["...500 texts batch..."]}
response: 502 Bad Gateway
worker: immediate retry (attempt 1) -> 502
worker: immediate retry (attempt 2) -> 502
worker: immediate retry (attempt 3) -> 502
```
We didn't expect retries to keep charging us for the same batch.

Maya (Infra): Looking at platform telemetry for acct_01G7x — I can see lots of repeated embedding requests with identical payload sizes and timestamps that line up with your worker retries. Two things: 1) our billing counts each API call that fully reaches the embeddings service (each retry is billed), and 2) your worker is doing immediate synchronous retries without exponential backoff, so failures turned into many billed attempts. Are you using SDK auto-retry or a custom loop?

Alejandro (SRE): To add — if a retry is triggered after the server partially accepted a batch (edge cases), you can end up double-processing. We can trace request_ids if you added an idempotency header (X-Request-ID) per batch. If not, we can still audit logs but it's slower. Sending a query to the logs now.

Sam (Support): Next steps for mitigation: 1) Stop or pause the background job to prevent more burn. 2) Push a quick patch to disable immediate retries (set max_retries=1) and add exponential_backoff with jitter. 3) Reduce batch size (e.g., from 500 -> 50) while we investigate. 4) If possible, add an idempotency header (X-Request-ID) so we can dedupe retries server-side. We'll perform a billing audit and issue credits for verified overcharge. Can you confirm you can pause the job?

Jill (Acme): I've paused the indexing queue and pushed a small change to the worker: max_retries=2, exponential backoff (base 200ms), jitter enabled, batch_size=50. Added X-Request-ID UUID per batch. Patch link (internal): https://redwood.internal/patch/4321 — please let me know if you need anything else to run the audit.

Maya (Infra): Thanks — seeing the pause. On our side, I can pull the embedding request traces for the window and look for duplicate payloads and request_ids. That will speed up the billing review. Quick note for the team: retries on embeddings/rerank are common cause of unexpected credit consumption — guidance lives here: https://docs.redwood.ai/inference/retries (internal docs).

Sam (Support): I escalated to Billing & SRE. We'll run the audit against the 02:00-05:00 UTC window and target a reply by EOD with the proposed credit. For immediate diagnostic: can you paste an example X-Request-ID you used so we can search quickly?

Jill (Acme): Example X-Request-ID: 9f14b2a6-3c4d-4a7c-b1e2-2d9f8a7c0b1f — that should match a few batches during the spike.

Alejandro (SRE): Found matching traces for that request-id: three attempts, all returned 502. Each attempt reached the embeddings worker and was billed. We'll include this in the audit. Recommendation for long-term: add client-side dedupe (check if uuid already processed) and prefer smaller batches with retries gated by exponential backoff + circuit breaker.

Jill (Acme): Understood — thanks for the quick help. One last question: does the free-trial auto-refund or do you apply manual credits?

Sam (Support): We don't auto-refund. Billing will review and apply manual credits to your account for verified overage. I'll update TKT-4321 with findings and the credit amount once audit completes. Thanks for patching the worker — that will stop further burn. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: TKT-4321 updated: audit in progress.

Jill (Acme): Appreciated. I'll keep the job paused until you confirm.

Sam (Support): Sounds good — keeping the ticket open. Expect another update by EOD.
